item.title: Quay.io Intermittent HTTP 502 on Pull/Push [postmortem]
item.description: On May 9, a surge of concurrent automated image pushes caused database lock contention that degraded Quay.io for approximately 18 minutes. Both image pushes and pulls returned errors during this window. The team identified and disabled an internal feature that amplified the contention, restoring service. We are redesigning this feature to operate asynchronously and improving our database locking mechanisms to better handle high-concurrency traffic.

item.title: Quay.io HTTP 502 on Pull/Push [postmortem]
item.description: On May 7, a production deployment introduced a database locking conflict that caused Quay.io to become unhealthy. Image pulls were intermittently degraded for approximately 30 minutes and image pushes were unavailable for approximately 3 hours. The team failed over to a secondary region to restore pulls, then reverted the deployment to fully restore service. We are implementing multi-phase deployment rollouts, stricter canary processes, and health probe improvements to prevent recurrence.

item.title: Quay.io Push/Pull Degraded [postmortem]
item.description: On April 21, a routine production deployment included a dependency upgrade that exposed a latent incompatibility, causing Quay.io application pods to crash on startup. Image pulls and pushes were fully unavailable for approximately 12 minutes before the team failed over to a secondary region, restoring pulls. Pushes remained unavailable for approximately 70 additional minutes while the deployment was reverted and traffic was incrementally shifted back to the primary region. We are enabling staging parity for all runtime features, improving automated rollback mechanisms, and isolating observability subsystems from the critical request path to prevent recurrence.

item.title: quay.io API failures [postmortem]
item.description: On March 30, 2026, Quay.io experienced a service disruption affecting image pulls and pushes, caused by an unexpected burst of resource-intensive operations that temporarily overloaded our primary database. Our engineering team mitigated the issue by failing over read traffic, restoring image pull capabilities within 45 minutes, and subsequently restored full push functionality once the database stabilized. We have since implemented enhanced traffic filtering and are actively optimizing our systems to prevent this from happening in the future.
